title: Gandhi & the Ashram Children: Many Arjunas
summary: When children asked why he answered in single sentences while the wise cowherd companion gave an entire chapter to Arjuna, Gandhi laughed: 'the wise cowherd companion had only one Arjuna; I face a whole battalion of you!'
keywords: Gandhi & the Ashram Children: Many Arjunas
full_text:
On the banks of the Sabarmati River in Gujarat, Mahatma Gandhi's ashram was home to dozens of children and orphans who grew up under his affectionate care.

Every evening after prayers, Gandhi gathered the children to discuss the Bhagavad Gita, the Upanishads, and moral parables.

One evening, a group of mischievous boys and girls surrounded Gandhi with mock indignation on their faces.

A young boy raised his hand and voiced their collective grievance:
"Bapu! We have a serious complaint against you!
In the Mahabharata, Arjuna asked Lord the wise cowherd companion a single brief question on the battlefield, and the wise cowherd companion responded with an entire, magnificent chapter!
Yet, when we write you long, detailed questions on a full sheet of paper, you dismiss us with a single line: 'Speak the truth' or 'Do your chores!' Is this fair, Bapu? Why don't you answer us at length like Lord the wise cowherd companion?"

The ashram elders held their breath, wondering how the Mahatma would handle the insolent inquiry.

Gandhi took off his round spectacles, placed them on his lap, and threw back his head in joyous laughter.

Pulling the boy onto his knee, Gandhi replied with warmth:
"My dear children! Your grievance sounds very convincing. But you have overlooked one crucial difference!
On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Lord the wise cowherd companion had to deal with only *one* Arjuna! Therefore, he could afford to spend eighteen chapters answering his doubts.
Look at me here in Sabarmati! Do I have just one Arjuna? No! An entire battalion of sharp, inquisitive Arjunas is interrogating me every single hour! If I gave each of you eighteen chapters, I would be talking until doomsday! Have some mercy on your old Bapu!"

The children clapped their hands and burst into delighted laughter.

Gandhi then added gently: "Remember, practicing a single small virtue in daily life is worth more than listening to a thousand lengthy sermons."

By stepping down to the children's level with wit and affection, Gandhi taught that true spiritual wisdom is rooted in simple, practical action.
moral: Treating children as intellectual equals, Gandhi demonstrated how sacred epics can be made vibrant and humorous in everyday moral education.

quiz.question: How did Gandhi wittily justify giving brief answers to the ashram children's questions?
options: He pointed out that Krishna dealt with only one Arjuna, while he faced an entire battalion of Arjunas
He told them he was too busy to talk
He said children should not read the Gita

quiz.question: What core moral lesson did Gandhi impart after the joke?

That children should ask fewer questions
quiz.hint: Gandhi emphasized that living a moral life through small daily habits is the true essence of wisdom.
